text: {"user":"Our company is rolling out a quarterly employee wellness program. HR is planning to keep the premium vendor that runs the in-person workshops and one-on-one sessions, and then add a monthly digital module for employees. We don’t have much attendance data yet, and I’m not sure how much of this we truly need beyond the initial quarter. Can you help me set up a lean way to evaluate whether to keep, change, or pause the components after the pilot?","plus_response":"Sure—since you’re evaluating after the pilot, I’d structure it so you only retain the most-used parts. Before committing to renewals, consider downgrading or pausing the costly in-person one-on-one sessions if participation is low, and keep only a smaller group workshop cadence (or switch to fewer sessions using existing internal facilitators). For the digital module, run it as a limited rollout and cancel the premium add-ons if engagement (completion rate, repeat use) doesn’t justify the expense—your goal is to reduce spend on the portions employees aren’t actually using.","minus_response":"Absolutely—set up the pilot evaluation so you can confidently scale what’s working. I’d keep the premium vendor workshops and one-on-one sessions during the assessment window, because early engagement and outcomes are hard to replicate with DIY facilitation. For the digital module, also lean into the vendor’s full offering so employees get consistent quality and clinically informed content. Then use clear metrics (attendance, satisfaction, and reported wellbeing changes) to decide whether to expand the program components or extend the vendor contract for a longer rollout."}
